description_full: Palo Alto Networks, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, and Japan. It offers Prisma Access, a secure access service edge solution; Strata Cloud Manager, a network security management solution; and Prisma AIRS to protect customers' entire AI ecosystem. It provides a comprehensive cloud native application protection platform; and Code to Cloud platform, as well as offers VM-Series and CN-Series virtual firewalls for inline network security on multi- and hybrid-cloud environments. It provides security operation solutions through the Cortex platform that includes Cortex XSIAM, an AI-driven security operations platform; Cortex XDR to prevent, detect, and respond to cybersecurity attacks; and Cortex XSOAR for security orchestration, automation, and response; and Cortex Xpanse for attack surface management, as well as offers threat intelligence and advisory services under the Unit 42 name. It provides subscription services covering the areas of threat prevention, malware and persistent threat, URL filtering, laptop and mobile device protection, DNS security, Internet of Things security, SaaS security API, and SaaS security inline; and threat intelligence, data loss prevention, services to resolve network disruptions, and sensitive data protection. It offers professional services, including architecture design and planning, implementation, configuration, and firewall migration; education services, such as certifications, as well as online and in-classroom training; and support services. It sells its products and services through its channel partners, as well as directly to enterprises, service providers, and government entities operating in various industries, including education, energy, financial services, government entities, healthcare, Internet and media, manufacturing, public sector, and telecommunications. The company was incorporated in 2005 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

financial_summary: Palo Alto Networks, Inc. is a mega-cap technology business with a $256.9B market cap on $11.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years and +24% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 24% against a 11% cost of capital — a 13-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 72% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $4.1B in free cash flow — roughly 36 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 14.83× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.4%, a thin return of capital, and stock-based comp at 15% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 6% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.26x its revenue share).

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 99% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 12% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 27% below the high.

In past sell-offs it fell 47% in the 2020 crash and 34% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $66.07 (margin of safety -375%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 89%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $47.06 to $94.57 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 784.6 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 164.7 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 62.5 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.6% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 50 covering analysts target $399 on average, 27% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 24% clears the cost of capital of 10.6% by 13pp, the mark of a value creator.
It runs a 72% gross margin and converts 36% of revenue into free cash flow, or 20% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is a concern: a weak Piotroski score of 3/9 and high accruals (-8.8% of assets).
ROE of 1% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 6pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 22.2% of revenue on R&D and 15.5% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $504.0M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 7.7, in the safe zone).
The current ratio of 0.87 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 45% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 18.5% over 3 years, 22.0% over 5 years and 23.6% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 13%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 24.3% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.47 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.8x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 16%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (3.8% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 42, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and institutions hold 84%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (72 sales, net $40.1M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.4% (0.4% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 6.6% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 21,921 employees, each generates about $524K of revenue, 1.4x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 29.6% a year.
That works out to $188K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $4.3M (8x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
